lyrics:
[Intro: three bass notes, climbing guitar figure, finger snaps]

[Verse 1: sweet tenor, bass and guitar only]
There's a puddle-jumper on my street
Yellow boots on both her feet
She turns a grey day gold
And she is four years old

[Chorus: harmony group joins, horns]
Ask me why I'm smiling
Ask me why I'm late
Sunshine in a raincoat
Swinging on my gate
(Sunshine) sunshine in a raincoat

[Verse 2: strings enter, drums fuller]
I've got pockets full of stones she found
I've got time now, I'm not city-bound
I don't need a thing they sell
I've got her hand in mine as well

[Chorus: harmony group, horns, strings]
Ask me why I'm smiling
Ask me why I'm late
Sunshine in a raincoat
Swinging on my gate
(Sunshine) sunshine in a raincoat

[Bridge: key lifts, strings play the guitar figure]
Hey, hey, hey
Hey, hey, hey

[Verse 3: higher key, everyone in]
I was tired and I was through
Ran out of things I meant to do
Then she said "Grandpa, look"
And that was all it took

[Final Chorus: full band, group ad-libbing]
Ask me why I'm smiling
Ask me why I'm late
Sunshine in a raincoat
Swinging on my gate
(Sunshine) sunshine in a raincoat

[Outro: guitar figure, snaps, voices fading]
Sunshine, sunshine
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 104 BPM, 4/4, C major, lifting a step for the last verse. An easy, strolling soul groove. Warm and contented.

VOICE: A male tenor with a sweet, slightly raspy, relaxed delivery. Four more men sing behind him in close harmony, with a deep bass voice at the bottom and a falsetto at the top, answering 'sunshine' and ad-libbing at the end.

INSTRUMENTS: An electric bass that opens the song alone with three notes. A clean electric guitar playing a short climbing figure. Finger snaps. A drum kit with a light backbeat. A horn section from the first chorus. A string section from the second verse, which later plays the guitar figure. Tambourine.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, bass, guitar figure and snaps. 0:10 Verse 1. 0:30 Chorus 1, voices and horns. 0:52 Verse 2, strings. 1:12 Chorus 2. 1:34 Bridge, the key lifts while the strings play the figure. 1:46 Verse 3 in the higher key. 2:06 Final chorus. 2:28 Outro, the guitar figure with fading voices to 2:42.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Mid-1960s Detroit soul: warm, clear and layered, each new instrument easy to hear as it arrives.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The three bass notes and the guitar figure in the first five seconds.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: 'My girl' is a granddaughter. The singer is retired, has time, and carries the stones she finds. The original's sweetness belongs at least as much to that kind of love.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Contentment, gratitude, joy.
